card.name: Subject right before "should be" instructions
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject noun phrase, often a drug name or its final piece, just before "should be" (stopped, monitored, discontinued). It appears in label warnings about monitoring or stopping treatment.

modes.label: End of drug brand name
modes.description: Final piece of a brand or drug name that is the subject of "should be discontinued/interrupted".

modes.label: Generic noun subject
modes.description: A drug class, dosage form or lab term ending the subject before "should be" administered or assessed.
modes.example: intranasal decongest<<ants>> should be administered at least 1 hour

modes.label: Joining word before a second action
modes.description: A joining word such as "and" or a registered mark where the sentence moves on to a "should be" clause.

card.writes: It prepares the model for a "should be" style verb and suppresses "will" in several languages.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label's subject ends and an instruction like "should be stopped" comes next.
